title: Supersoldat français — armure futuriste et mégalopole en ruine
prompt:
Photorealistic sci-fi power-armored supersoldier, French-inspired, standing in a silent ruined megacity. The armor is monolithic and seamless like a single-piece precision shell: anodized ceramic-aluminum composite, pearl white base with oil-slick iridescence that shifts cyan→magenta→gold at grazing angles. Surfaces are impossibly clean yet subtly micro-scratched, with soft radii and perfect chamfers; every seam is a hairline shadow. French identity is encoded as micro-engraved fleur-de-lis patterns only visible in specular highlights, and a tiny tricolor enamel inlay—no cloth, no clutter, pure industrial elegance.
Then the “acid” hits: volumetric light fractures into prismatic caustics across the armor, as if the air is made of glass; faint holographic glyphs ripple like heat mirages, bending perspective. The soldier holds a brutal sci-fi rifle that looks impossibly simplified—a clean block with hidden mechanics—yet still menacing. Background: collapsed Eiffel Tower silhouette in fog, distant embers, low thunderclouds.
Cinematic photography: full-frame DSLR, 85mm, f/1.8, ISO 200, shallow depth of field, high micro-contrast, ultra-detailed materials, soft rim light + neon spectral bounce, subtle film grain, HDR but natural, no cartoon look, no anime.

title: Paysage alpin miniature dans une bouteille
prompt: A photorealistic image of a clear glass bottle standing on a dark wood office desk, captured like a high-end product photo in a modern workspace. Inside the bottle is an entire miniature alpine mountain landscape with towering snow-dusted peaks, jagged rocky cliffs, dense evergreen forests, and a crystal-clear lake reflecting the mountains, all rendered with extreme surface detail and texture. The dark wooden desk surface shows fine grain, subtle wear, and soft reflections of the bottle, with a blurred suggestion of office items and a monitor in the background to imply a real desk environment. Depth of field is shallow, with the front edge of the bottle and the central mountain range in perfect sharp focus, while the back of the desk and office background fall into a soft blur, emphasizing ultra-high resolution, crisp textures in rock, snow, bark, glass, and wood, with true-to-life colors, realistic shadows, and no stylization or painterly effects, in the style of professional commercial product photography

title: Personnage sortant de son image
prompt: Using the provided reference image, generate a dramatic image where the main character appears to break out of the original picture and come to life. Preserve the character’s identity, facial features, outfit, and overall style exactly as shown in the reference image. The original image should appear as physically cracking, tearing, or shattering from the inside as the character pushes through it.The character’s upper body and hands should emerge beyond the flat surface, transitioning from a two-dimensional image into a fully three-dimensional, living form. Fragments of the original image—such as paper tears—should fly outward, frozen mid-air for a cinematic effect. The character’s expression should convey determination, intensity, or awakening, as if gaining consciousness and stepping into the real world. Match the lighting, color palette, and textures of the character to the reference image, while enhancing realism and depth on the parts that break out of the frame. Use dramatic lighting with strong highlights and shadows to emphasize the transformation from image to reality. The background outside the original image should feel darker and more realistic, creating a strong contrast between the flat image world and the living, three-dimensional space. The final result should feel cinematic, dynamic, and powerful, clearly showing the moment the character escapes the image and becomes alive.

title: Traduction graphique d’une photo en formes
prompt:
Use the uploaded photo as the only visual source and create an artistic, graphic-design-oriented “shape translation” image.

Do not simply apply a filter to the photo, and do not fully redraw the original image.

First, extract the 2–4 most representative visual features from the original photo, such as texture, tonal variation, color gradient, light spots, ripples, edge flow, grain, natural rhythm, spatial direction, or repeating structure.

Do not preserve everything evenly. Actively remove secondary information and simplify the image to avoid visual clutter.

Then reorganize those visual elements and fill them into a clear silhouette of a biological or natural object.

The target silhouette should match the mood of the original photo as naturally as possible. For example:
ocean or water scenes → fish / whale / jellyfish
sky scenes → bird / cloud / butterfly
tree shadows or forest scenes → deer / tree / leaf

The final result should make the original photo still feel perceptible, while the overall image has clearly transformed into a new silhouette-based visual identity.

Style requirements:
artistic, restrained, quiet, with a modern graphic design feel.
Place the main subject on a large negative-space background in white, warm white, or very light grey.

Do not make it a plain silhouette or a realistic illustration.

Do not simply force the photo inside a shape. Preserve the internal flow of natural textures and layered visual structure.

Moderate slicing, repetition, misalignment, stepped edges, or frame-stacking effects are allowed to introduce a stronger graphic-design language.

Keep the composition clean and minimal, with the subject centered or near-center.

A slight grain, film texture, or subtle print texture is allowed.

The final result should feel like an art poster combining photography, graphic design, and visual translation.

The priority is not to copy the original photo, but to extract its most compelling structures and textures, then complete a visual transformation through a new silhouette.
